references.text: Ezekiel prophesied about God's promise to give His people a new heart and a new spirit – precisely the spiritual renewal that Jesus expected Nicodemus, as Israel's teacher, to know: "I will sprinkle clean water on you ... I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you" ([ref:Ezek 36:25-27|Ezekiel 36:25-27]).

Ezekiel's vision of the dry bones coming to life by the Spirit illustrates the spiritual rebirth that Jesus speaks about. God's Spirit gives life to what was dead ([ref:Ezek 37:1-14|Ezekiel 37:1-14]). An Israelite teacher should have understood this.

Jeremiah's prophecy of the new covenant, where God writes His law on hearts, points to the inner renewal Jesus speaks of. Nicodemus, as a scribe, should have known this promise ([ref:Jer 31:31-34|Jeremiah 31:31-34]).

Isaiah prophesied that God would pour out His Spirit on Israel's descendants: "I will pour water on the thirsty land and streams on the dry ground. I will pour out My Spirit on your offspring" ([ref:Isa 44:3|Isaiah 44:3]). This too is a promise Nicodemus should have known.

The parallel with the prologue: Jesus came to His own, but His own did not receive Him ([ref:John 1:10-11|John 1:10-11]). Nicodemus represents Israel's leaders who do not understand who Jesus is and what He teaches.

Paul refers to the Jews who were convinced they were guides for the blind and teachers of the foolish, yet did not teach themselves ([ref:Rom 2:20-21|Romans 2:20-21]). This mirrors Jesus' rebuke of Nicodemus as Israel's teacher.

"The natural person does not accept what pertains to God's Spirit, for it is foolishness to him, and he cannot understand it" ([ref:1 Cor 2:14|1 Corinthians 2:14]). Nicodemus' lack of understanding illustrates that spiritual truths require spiritual insight.

David's prayer for a clean heart and a new, steadfast spirit ([ref:Ps 51:12-14|Psalms 51:12-14]) points to the spiritual renewal Jesus speaks about – something an Israelite teacher should have understood from the Scriptures.

Nicodemus was a Pharisee and one of the Jewish rulers who came to Jesus at night ([ref:John 3:1-2|John 3:1-2]). As a leading teacher in Israel, he had access to the Scriptures, yet still did not understand spiritual rebirth.
